text:
sre-bot: 🔔 ALERT: multiple spot interruptions in us-west-2 affecting gpu-spot-nodepool-1. cluster-autoscaler reporting repeated scale-up/scale-down cycles. high queue backlog on inference pods
ivan: seeing 500+ pending pods with GPU requests, nodepool dwindling from 12 -> 4 in ~3m due to spot terminations :grimacing:
maya: confirmed. latency SLOs slipping on hosted API mostly for long-form generation routes
chris: cluster-autoscaler logs look like a thrash: it scales up, nodes get preempted, pods get backfilled, then scale down immediately. we should stop the downscales until backlog clears
devops-jen: recommended short term: increase `maxNodes` on on-demand fallback pool and set scaleDownUnneededTime to 10m to avoid immediate downsizing
oncall-alex: agree. also we can cordon the remaining spot nodes to prevent new scheduling while we stabilize
ivan: executing cordon on spot pool: `kubectl cordon node/gpu-spot-*-*`
ivan: draining non-critical jobs off spot nodes now (`kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`)
rachel: pushing a quick patch to autoscaler config to set `scaleDownDelayAfterAdd: 600s` and `expander: priority` — will apply to us-west-2 cluster now
chris: also toggle `balance-similar-node-groups: false` temporarily to reduce churning across nodegroups
maya: can we fail over critical workloads to the on-demand GPU pool? cost will spike but it's better than erroring requests
devops-jen: doing `kubectl label nodepool/gpu-on-demand fallback=true` and adding toleration to inference-deployment to accept fallback nodes. quick rollout with 2 replicas to start
ivan: running command to bump on-demand nodegroup desired: `aws eks update-nodegroup-config --cluster-name prod --nodegroup-name gpu-on-demand --scaling-config minSize=2,maxSize=12,desiredSize=6`
oncall-alex: noted some customers in APAC might be impacted if autoscaler decides cross-region fallback. keep routing local for now
rachel: applied autoscaler patch. logs: `I0901 12:34:56 autoscaler.go: scaleDownCandidates found, delaying scale down due to recent add` :thumbsup:
maya: monitoring dashboards show pending token queue dropping after on-demand bump. tailing logs show fewer OOMs too
ivan: postmortem action: add a node lifecycle hook that tags spot nodes for faster rebalancing? and set a higher `scaleUpCooldown` for spot pools
chris: long term: consider sticky scheduling for inference pods to prefer nodes with KV cache warmed (reduces token cost) and set a two-tier autoscaler policy (spot aggressive up, on-demand conservative)
devops-jen: another follow-up: add automation to detect >30% spot interruptions in a 5m window and auto-expand on-demand fallback with a budget cap
oncall-alex: customer comms: ops -> send brief incident note to incidents channel if user-facing error rate >1% in next hour
ivan: summary: cordoned spot nodes, drained non-critical pods, patched autoscaler config to delay scale-down, bumped on-demand pool to 6 desired, added short-term tolerations. observed backlog decreasing
maya: good work. create a ticket for the autoscaler policy experiment and cost guardrails. assign to eng-infra + eng-sre
chris: saving logs/snippets: ```
# autoscaler config diff
- scaleDownDelayAfterAdd: 10s
+ scaleDownDelayAfterAdd: 600s
- balanceSimilarNodeGroups: true
+ balanceSimilarNodeGroups: false
```
rachel: will open the follow-ups and include the metrics we tracked (pending pods, avg latency, spot interruption count) :spiral_notepad:
ivan: closing thread when backlog < 20 and error rate stable for 15m. will update here
sre-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: backlog cleared, scale events stabilized at 12:34:95 UTC. tagging for postmortem. :tada:
